title: Applied Science
intro: If water could speak, it would tell us everything it has carried. Applied Science is how I listen – connecting villages with the water they depend on, and that water with the natural compounds that can purify it.

blocks.text: Honored with national and international competitions, I’ve turned curiosity into research, and research into a compass pointing me towards communities in need – each award marking not just victory, but a step further along that path.

blocks.text: Exploring where science meets the community, my research bridges environmental chemistry, data, and policy – from microbes and nanomaterials to sensors and cities – each project a step toward turning understanding into care for the environment.

entry.alt: Trang đầu bài báo “Microbial Treatment of Polluted Water: Mechanisms, Treatment Strategies, Applications, and Future Perspectives”
entry.title: Bioremediation of Polluted Waters using Microorganisms | Co-Author

meta.label: Published:
meta.text: Journal of Scientific and Engineering Research

entry.text: I synthesized how microbes and constructed wetlands remove heavy metals, dyes, and other pollutants from water – comparing biosorption with biodegradation and exploring how AI and nanobiotechnology could scale them. Where microbes meet pollution, I turned scattered literature into a clearer path toward sustainable treatment.

entry.alt: Trang bài báo trên ScienceDirect: Green synthesis and characteristics of Ag-ZnO doped nanoparticles utilizing plant extracts as reducing agents
entry.title: Green-Synthesized Ag-ZnO Nanoparticles for Antibiotic Removal
entry.text: I assisted in synthesizing Ag-ZnO nanoparticles from lime juice and pomelo peel extracts, running tetracycline degradation trials under white LED light. Through this project, I explored how green chemistry can reimagine water treatment – giving new life to everyday plant materials through careful design.

entry.text: I extended my research beyond the lab paper and onto the page, taking apart the Ramsey Rule to argue that a century-long horizon calls for a discount rate, not a single fixed number. Rigor, for me, also means putting understanding into words – making a complex idea clear and connecting economics, ethics with the environment.

entry.text: I looked at my home city as an engineered system, and argued that sustainability must be designed from the start, so that cities adapt to growth rather than scramble to react to it.

blocks.text: Treatment System for Lead Removal from Household Battery Leakage

Transforming beakers and equations into tangible solutions, I design tools that give toxic metals nowhere to hide – systems that help households read what an old battery leaves behind, protect their water, and turn chemistry into quiet acts of change.

row.alt: Pin cũ rỉ sét nằm lẫn trong đất cạnh một cây rau non
row.note: In Vietnam, households often throw used batteries away with everyday waste – a quiet habit that lets toxic metals seep into the soil and water around us.

row.alt: Nhóm học sinh ngồi trên sàn lắp ráp mô hình thùng chứa pin
row.note: Recognizing this challenge, I led a team of three to prototype a five-layer containment unit for leaking batteries – sand and sawdust to absorb, baking soda to neutralize acid, activated carbon to capture lead – with a pH sensor that flags a leak early, before it can reach soil and water.

row.alt: Thùng nhựa trong chứa các lớp vật liệu lọc, trên nắp đặt pin cũ, gắn cảm biến
row.note: I introduced our product to households and schools, the places where old batteries pile up, and contemplated their feedback for further development.

row.alt: Khánh Chi và bạn trình bày sản phẩm bên poster trước ban giám khảo
row.note: After countless refinements born from field tests, I finalized the unit – a fusion of chemistry and sensing. I then brought it to the Vinschool Science & Innovation Challenge, presenting not just a product, but a vision of how humble materials can protect our soil and water.

row.alt: Đội thi cùng thầy cô chụp ảnh trên sân khấu VSIC 2026
row.note: Through three challenging rounds of presentations and evaluations, the project advanced to the final – where it was honored with the Special Prize, a recognition of the harmony between science and the soil and water it serves.

blocks.text: After diving deep into chemistry and research, I realized its wonder lies not in the lab but in the questions it sparks – even a child can grasp its magic. So I co-organized STEM classes under Youth for Community, bringing hands-on experiments to underprivileged and Dao ethnic students across Northern Vietnam, giving back what I've learned and inspiring young minds to explore the science around them.

blocks.text: Through Youth for Community, I taught STEM classes – translating non-Newtonian fluids, natural color indicators, and water rockets into wonder, inviting young minds to see science as the language of curiosity and possibility.

blocks.text: After teaching in small classrooms, I’m eager to see that science spark reaches more students. At the Vietnam STEM, AI and Robotics Championship, I organized a stage where students from across the country came to test their ideas, and co-managed the Water Rocket track, the same experiment I once taught to ethnic children, now launching from the hands of teams who built it themselves.

row.text: Beyond the experiments, I set out to change how youngsters approach the environment, as a shared responsibility. I helped organize X-Interval, turning experts’ knowledge about carbon and the energy transition into conversations that anyone could join and carry forward.

Whether in a workshop or at a community project site during Youth for Impact, I find the same spark in every student – hands raised with wonder, questions flowing about climate, education, and fairness. In their curiosity, I see my younger self, reciting all seventeen SDGs under my breath, tracing how those goals could one day reach the villages I came from.

blocks.text: Alongside achievements and research, I ventured into the world where chemistry becomes a working language – applying its precision and patience in a nanotechnology lab and a recycling social enterprise, where my creative designing ideas have to bend to the discarded materials and constraints.

blocks.text: In collaboration with Prof. Dr. Quoc Trung Vu and Prof Minh Duc Tran at the HNUE, I developed green adsorbents from fish scales and rice husks – pulling textile dyes and heavy metal ions out of water, then testing the method on real wastewater from Thuong Tin’s craft villages.

blocks.text: Stepping into the chemistry lab at HNUE, I was filled with anticipation and curiosity. The air buzzed with the promise of discovery, and I was eager to immerse myself in the world where science meets untreated water.

Khánh Chi đeo khẩu trang vẽ trang trí lên tấm kính tái chế

blocks.text: As an intern at Red River Recycling, a recycling social enterprise, I met Mr. Duc, its founder, worked beside him through the whole life of discarded glass and plastic – sorting it, processing it into raw material, treating it to be safe, and shaping it into decorative pieces. Through this opportunity, I glimpsed the maker's perspective: how to read a material and let it decide its final form – whether through the patience of sorting or the surprise of shaping.
